newsitem.title: ITALY: TIM, Omnitel even in Italian 1996 GSM race.
newsitem.headline: TIM, Omnitel even in Italian 1996 GSM race.

text.p: Italy's two mobile phone operators Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) and Omnitel, the consortium controlled by Olivetti, are neck and neck in enrolling subscribers for their GSM digital system so far in 1996.
TIM has 52.5 percent of new subscribers during the first nine months while Omnitel's share was 47.5 percent, Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported.
However, in the third quarter of 1996 Omnitel saw greater growth than its rival, gaining 260,000 new GSM subscribers against TIM's 248,000.

A TIM spokeswoman put its latest GSM subscriber numbers at 1.1 million in mid-October, while its total mobile phone subscribers were very close to 5 million -- this number includes GSM digital and analogue network subscribers.
TIM launched its GSM service in early 1995 and gained 468,000 subscribers by end-1995, some 773,000 by end-June 1996 and 1.021 million by end-September 1996.
Omnitel launched its own GSM service in December 1995 reached 60,000 by end of 1995, some 300,000 by end-June 1996 and 560,000 by end-September.
Omnitel's latest forecasts are to reach 700,000 GSM subscribers by the end of the year, after it had only forecast 400,000 by end-1996 at the beginning of the year.
